items.summary: Remote desktop, terminal, file transfer, port forwarding and VPN in a single app; give Claude Code, Codex or similar a Markdown skill and the agent drives another machine through the rds command line — runs commands, reads screenshots, clicks, copies files and opens port forwards. Connections are peer-to-peer over QUIC + TLS 1.3, with relays only when hole punching fails; available on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS and the web.
items.title: RockDesk: a remote desktop built for AI agents — one sentence lets yours drive your other machines (Show HN, Nov 18)

items.summary: Each turn advances through an event-driven state machine, with every conversation and tool call recorded in an immutable SQLite event log that supports branching and backtracking; the same runtime powers a desktop app and a CLI, can be deployed to a remote host over SSH, and supports scheduled tasks and Slack, Discord and Telegram gateways, with 40+ models to choose from.
items.title: Pizza: an event-driven open-source AI agent, no while true loop (Show HN, Nov 15)

items.summary: One command installs a crew of AI specialists on a single Debian/Ubuntu machine: they answer messages, chase quotes, book visits and keep the paperwork in order, each with its own job, and ask you before anything important. Tasks, documents, semantic memory, a model gateway and the Studio operator panel all stay local, and the model can be Claude, GPT, Gemini or a local one.
items.title: Smart Node: a self-hosted AI crew that runs the front office on a machine you own (open-sourced Nov 12, AGPL-3.0)
